symptom: On MPR v2 nearly every command opened most unit files in a fresh process: on a 4,753-unit app `show modules` 4,511, `describe microflow` 2,996, `describe page` 3,176, `show microflows in M` 3,072. Fast enough on macOS, a per-call floor of seconds on Windows, where Defender scans each open
cause: A unit's Name lives only in its BSON, and the type index (mendixlabs/mxcli#1603) held only $Type. The container hierarchy read every Projects$Folder for its name; `getMicroflowNames` / `ListMicroflowHeaders` read every microflow for Name and Excluded; `ListMicroflowsNamed` filtered every microflow on the stored Name; a page describe's `flowReturnEntity` decoded every microflow per flow-sourced widget; `show modules` decoded seven document types to count them; `populateViewEntityOql` listed every module per view-entity document
file: `modelsdk/mpr/reader_units_v2.go` (index entry: Type, Name, Excluded; file `unit-index-2.idx`), `modelsdk/mpr/reader_units.go` (`ListUnitHeaders`), `modelsdk/mpr/types.go` (`ListFolders`), `modelsdk/mprread/generic.go` (`ListUnitHeaders`, `ListUnitsNamed`), `mdl/executor/cmd_modules.go` (`listModules` counts by unit type plus `meta` System built-ins), `mdl/executor/helpers.go` (`microflowsInModule`), `mdl/executor/cmd_pages_describe_flowcontext.go`, `mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel.go`
insight: **Trace reads by caller, not by count.** A temporary hook in `readMprContents` that records the unit's $Type and the first non-reader frames gave a table like `1908 Microflows$Microflow <- ListMicroflowHeaders < getMicroflowNames` per command, which named every fix directly; the raw count only said 'too many'. Anything derived from a unit's top level belongs in the ContentsHash index beside its type: it cannot go stale for the same reason. **Changing a persisted cache's format needs a new file name, not only a new header**: the old and new binaries each read the other's file as corrupt, rebuilt it and wrote their own, so two mxcli versions on one project (VS Code extension plus CLI) reopened every file on every call. That showed up only as nonsense numbers while benchmarking old against new on one project. Counting from unit types missed the System module's built-in enumerations and Java actions, which the listings add from `modelsdk/meta`; an agreement test against the full listings caught it (System Enums 0 vs 15). Guards: `TestFreshProcess_CommandsOpenOnlyWhatTheyShow` (pedapp: 196/113 reads before, 56/18 after), `TestShowModules_CountsAgreeWithTheListings`, `TestListUnitHeaders_*`, `TestUnitIndex_PreviousFormatIsLeftAlone`
